purpose: Checker Mode D (D-024) for x18a-login-both-directions: drive AutoTester's OWN UI in a real headless Chromium against a served copy of tests/fixtures/spa_login_site, to prove the crawl page and crawls table show login_failed (non-success tone) for a wrong password and completed (positive tone) for a correct password -- never reading the maker's screenshots, never substituting curl.

setup.site_served: tests/fixtures/spa_login_site (from an isolated throwaway copy of the tree at build commit e70bb2c, python http.server on an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port)
setup.ui: autotester.ui.app:app via uvicorn, isolated AUTOTESTER_ROOT (never the bound worktree's own projects/), synthetic project 'demo'
setup.driver: playwright.sync_api, chromium headless=True, launched from the checker's own script -- the playwright MCP was unavailable (connection failure) so a standalone uv run python script was used instead, per dispatch instructions
setup.note_on_first_attempt: A first run hung ~20 minutes with near-zero CPU (0.64s user+kernel over 21 min wall) and no crawl ever landing on disk. Root-caused to uvicorn's subprocess.PIPE stdout filling the OS pipe buffer with request logs while nothing drained it, blocking the server's own response thread. Fixed by redirecting the UI server's stdout/stderr to a real log file instead of a PIPE, adding explicit small crawl bounds, and wrapping the whole run in a 280s hard `timeout`. The stuck processes (uvicorn + its python children) were verified by command line and killed before retrying; a SECOND leftover uvicorn from the fixed run (Windows detaches `uv run uvicorn`'s real process from the Popen handle, so `ui_proc.terminate()` did not reach it) was found and killed the same way afterward -- both cleanups are logged in the checker's own session, not this file's data.

note_on_first_mode_d_report: An earlier version of this report (produced by the initial script, before the row-parsing was scoped exactly to a <tr>) flagged 'crawls_table_row_has_wrong_badge_class: true' for the correct-password row -- a false alarm from an 800-char substring window that bled from the correct-password row into the adjacent wrong-password row's badge-blocked class. Re-verified directly against the same persisted crawl data with a proper <tr>...</tr> regex (shown above as crawls_table_row_exact for each row): each row carries exactly one badge class, matching its own status. Recorded here so this evidence file explains the discrepancy rather than silently replacing it.
conclusion: X18(a)/X18(c) verified live end-to-end through the actual product UI: a crawl started from the Crawls page with a wrong-password login case reads login_failed with a non-success (warning) tone on both the crawl page and the crawls table; the same flow with a correct password reads completed with a positive tone. Zero console errors on either page.
